method.question: Would approved/current Mission 0 English fit local source byte budgets if each English character occupied one byte instead of two-byte fullwidth Shift-JIS?
method.english_projection: ASCII-compatible one-byte length after normalizing common typographic punctuation to ASCII equivalents
limitations: This is a storage-capacity calculation only; it does not prove parser safety, control-byte safety, pointer safety, or renderer support.
Aggregate surplus in one resource class cannot be pooled with deficit in another unless relocation ownership and pointers are independently proven.

The previously reported 497/502 fullwidth cohort could not be reconstructed exactly from current main or the recovered project artifacts, so no result below is presented as the same 502-record cohort.

historical_reference.reported_prior_result: 497/502 do not fit under two-byte fullwidth encoding
historical_reference.comparison_status: directionally superseded but not numerically apples-to-apples

review_workbook.interpretation: The old two-byte/fullwidth warning materially overstated the storage problem. A one-byte renderer converts hundreds of previously impossible local fits into viable same-size fits, although dialogue still has a real local-capacity deficit.

current_master_script.interpretation: The current script is somewhat more verbose than the older review workbook, but the same conclusion holds: one-byte encoding reduces the problem substantially without eliminating per-record/per-resource relocation needs.
